title: Trivial Assemblers (Conversion-Only Classes)
pattern: Defining a dedicated class, struct, or service that contains no state and no behavior other than mapping fields between two types (typically Entity and DTO).
why_bad: It adds useless class ceremony and indirection. Converting between types is an operation, not a standalone architectural component. Exposing this via a custom class forces developers to import and inject a useless helper rather than using language-native conversions.
detection: A stateless struct or class containing only type mapping functions, with no other business responsibilities.
counterexample: Assemblers that combine and parse complex data from multiple distinct systems (like aggregating user profiles, transaction logs, and security checks) to produce a unified API response.
source: Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (2002), p. 401.
